correctness.rationale: For m≥3, two hubwise unit prices p≤q and budget B>0 on K_(2,m), concavity of λ₂ in edge conductances permits averaging over leaf permutations without decreasing the unrestricted optimum. The hub-constant u,v matrix has nonzero eigenvalues s=u+v (mult. m−1) and roots of z²−(m+1)sz+m(m+2)uv. Requiring λ₂≥1 is equivalent to s≥1 and uv≥((m+1)s−1)/(m(m+2)); at fixed s the cheaper allocation uses the minimal admissible expensive-hub weight v=(s−sqrt(D(s)))/2. With D=(s−a)²−b², strict convexity of m[ps+(q−p)v(s)] for p<q yields the exact switch at sqrt(q/p)+sqrt(p/q)=m²−2, both explicit C* branches, positive symmetric optimizers and Fiedler multiplicities m versus 1. The p=q continuum s=1, uv≥1/(m+2) is treated separately. Independent sympy exact spectral factorizations in three dimensions and 70 price/parameter combinations corroborated the analytic optimization.

These primary sources describe methods or different graph/price models rather than an explicit two-price all-m K_(2,m) optimum, sharp price-ratio threshold or multiplicity change. A published semantic hit about complete-bipartite symmetric-edge polytopes concerns an entirely different graph, not this priced-Laplacian design. More specialist historical dual formulations remain possible.

value.rationale: The result solves a natural cost-asymmetric network-conductance design family in closed form with a sharp price-induced change in the active spectral bottleneck and dimension of Fiedler eigenspace, supplying structural guidance and avoiding a numerical SDP for each budget. The all-m phase boundary is a motivated exact invariant, not merely an unpriced standard spectrum.
